competitors.name: mean_reversion
competitors.rules: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.

competitors.name: You
competitors.rules: Your real Robinhood account, rebased to the shared origin so it's comparable. Performance only — holdings and trades are deliberately not published.

competitors.name: congress_mirror
competitors.rules: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

regime.label: Strong growth, restrictive rates, elevated inflation
regime.note: The Federal Reserve held the federal-funds target at 3.75%-4.00% on October 28, described activity as expanding at a strong pace and inflation as elevated, and recorded two dissents favoring a 25 bp hike. Low confidence and 70% cash reflect policy risk, binary event risk, and the book's weak long-run record.

analyst.thesis: Carry forward the concentrated event book rather than chase the screen's leveraged and overbought leaders. tools/analyst_memory.py reports the analyst book at $84.81, with -18.1 points of all-time alpha and a -3.13 annualized Sharpe, despite +0.8 points of alpha on the latest recorded tick. VRTX gained 3.50% on the October 30 settled session and has two confirmed catalysts: Q3 results after the November 2 close and the November 30 povetacicept PDUFA date. The market expects $4.70 of Q3 EPS according to Robinhood; the differentiated view is that updated Crinetics integration guidance and continued renal-pipeline execution can preserve value beyond the earnings print, while the 18% weight contains binary risk. MSFT fell 1.55% on October 30 despite FY27 Q1 revenue growth of 19% and Azure growth of 48%; Microsoft Ignite runs November 17-20. The differentiated view is that product detail at Ignite can support monetization expectations before another earnings confirmation. Hold 18% VRTX, 12% MSFT, and 70% cash. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve said it maintained the target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, economic activity was expanding at a strong pace, and inflation remained elevated; two members preferred a 1/4-point increase.
Vertex confirmed Q3 2026 results for November 2 after the close with a 4:30 p.m. ET call; Robinhood's calendar showed a $4.70 EPS estimate.
Vertex said the FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date for povetacicept and that approval would make it the first commercial therapy in Vertex's nephrology franchise.

Robinhood showed VRTX at 32.514763x trailing earnings, Q2 revenue of $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income of $1.0998 billion, and 12.45% year-over-year revenue growth; REGN traded at 20.484444x and LLY at 46.570320x.
Microsoft's filed FY27 Q1 results showed revenue of $92.279 billion versus $77.673 billion, up 19%, and Azure revenue of $33.165 billion versus $22.384 billion, up 48%.
Microsoft says Ignite takes place November 17-20, 2026 in San Francisco and online, focused on AI, cloud, security, and data.
Robinhood showed MSFT at 27.256348x trailing earnings, FY27 Q1 net margin of 39.69%, and 18.80% year-over-year revenue growth.
On October 30, settled closes moved 3.50% for VRTX, -1.55% for MSFT, and -1.77% for SPY.

risks: VRTX Q3 results after the November 2 close can reset guidance and expectations before the FDA decision.
VRTX has binary November 30 regulatory risk; delay, rejection, a restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation invalidates the anchor thesis.
At 32.514763x trailing earnings, VRTX carries a premium to REGN at 20.484444x and needs pipeline execution to justify it.
Microsoft Ignite may add no financially material information, and AI infrastructure spending can pressure margins despite strong Azure growth.
The book has -18.1 points of all-time alpha and a -3.13 Sharpe; two positive relative ticks do not justify high confidence.
A 70% cash balance creates opportunity cost if risk assets rally.

rationale.VRTX: [DATA] VRTX closed October 30 at $558.88, up 3.50% for the session. Vertex confirmed Q3 results after the November 2 close and the November 30 povetacicept PDUFA date. Robinhood reported 32.514763x P/E, Q2 revenue of $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income of $1.0998 billion, and 12.45% year-over-year revenue growth. [ASSUMED] Updated Crinetics integration guidance and a favorable FDA decision can establish a nephrology and endocrine growth platform faster than the market credits. Earnings and FDA binary risk, plus poor long-run book alpha, cap the weight at 18%.
rationale.MSFT: [DATA] Microsoft's FY27 Q1 filing reported revenue of $92.279 billion versus $77.673 billion, Azure revenue of $33.165 billion versus $22.384 billion, and 39.69% net margin. MSFT closed October 30 at $521.91, down 1.55%. Robinhood reported 27.256348x trailing P/E. Microsoft Ignite runs November 17-20. [ASSUMED] Strong cloud growth plus a near-dated roadmap event offers a cleaner anticipatory setup than the screen's overbought winners, but the event may be financially immaterial, so size at 12%.

reflection.looking_back: The carried book entered the tick with 18% VRTX, 12% MSFT, and 70% cash. tools/analyst_memory.py reports the latest recorded tick at +0.5% for the book versus -0.3% for SPY, about +0.8 points of alpha; on the October 30 settled session VRTX gained 3.50%, MSFT lost 1.55%, and SPY lost 1.77%.
worked: VRTX gained 3.50% on October 30 while retaining confirmed November 2 and November 30 catalysts.
The latest recorded book tick beat SPY by about 0.8 points.
missed: MSFT lost 1.55% on October 30, so the pre-Ignite position has not yet delivered absolute return.
The positive relative tick does not repair -18.1 points of all-time alpha or the -3.13 Sharpe.
reflection.adjustment: Hold VRTX and MSFT at existing weights rather than add into binary earnings risk; keep 70% cash until the event outcomes or sustained alpha justify more exposure.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 111 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
